pl-l4d41c1-d1e115.summary: Quotes Gregory on affinity, the kinship that belongs to the husband through his wife or to the wife through her husband: since by God's sentence I and my wife are one flesh, her kin and mine become one kinship to me; so I and my wife's sister are in the first degree, her son in the second, her granddaughter in the third, and so on both ways; a relative's wife is to be treated as a woman of my own kin in that degree; those who think otherwise are antichrists.
claims: Affinity follows from the spouses' one flesh.
A spouse's kin stand to the other in the same degree.

pl-l4d41c1-d1e124.summary: Cites Pope Julius: a man is joined equally to his own kin and his wife's kin.

pl-l4d41c1-d1e130.summary: Cites Isidore: consanguinity to be kept in one's own husband must be kept in the wife's kin by the law of marriage, since they were two in one flesh, so both kinships are common to them.
claims: Both spouses' kinships are common to them.

pl-l4d41c1-d1e137.summary: Adds Julius: we permit no one of either sex to marry from his own or his wife's blood kin to the seventh degree, since as no Christian may marry within his own kin, so neither within his wife's, because of the unity of flesh.
claims: Affinity forbids marriage to the seventh degree.

pl-l4d41c1-d1e146.summary: Cites Gregory: affinity is to be observed through the degrees of kinship to the seventh generation, as inheritance extends succession to the seventh degree.
claims: Affinity extends to the seventh degree, like inheritance.

pl-l4d41c1-d1e155.summary: Concludes that these authorities show what affinity is and to which degree it must be observed, the seventh.

pl-l4d41c1.summary: Turns to affinity, the kinship that comes to a husband from his wife's side and to a wife from her husband's. Gregory: since husband and wife are one flesh, each's kin become kin to the other in the same degree, so a wife's sister is in the first degree to the husband; those who think otherwise are antichrists. Julius and Isidore confirm that a man must treat his wife's kin as his own, and Gregory extends affinity to the seventh generation, as inheritance extends to the seventh degree.
claims: Affinity arises because husband and wife are one flesh.
A spouse's kin are kin to the other in the same degree.
Affinity is observed to the seventh degree.
